targets.text: qodo-cli is a bridge: one app with an HTTP API, an MCP server and an embeddable web surface, built on a reusable bridge framework. culture-rules drives it through an actor, so a rule runs Qodo when a PR is opened and another has a cortex agent improve the repo's Qodo configuration when a PR is merged. No extra repo was created.
Both flows run end to end on a real PR with culture-rules holding only configuration, and no repository was created.
qodo-cli gains a server (HTTP API), an MCP server and a web UI, and its command is named qodo-cli. None of the three exists today: the only network code is the urllib call in qodo/cli/_qodo_api.py.
qodo serve starts the API and the web UI from an installed wheel with no Node on the machine, and qodo mcp serves the same verbs as tools.

qodo-cli's runtime dependencies stay empty (pyproject.toml dependencies = [], best_practices.md:11-14). The server, MCP and web parts sit behind optional extras and are imported lazily, as culture-rules does with its server and mcp extras.
pip install qodo-cli with no extras installs zero third-party packages and every existing verb still works.

Every new qodo-cli verb keeps the existing contract (CLAUDE.md:61-64, 159-167): --json, CliError, exit codes 0/1/2, an explain catalog entry, mentions in learn and overview, and teken cli doctor --strict green. Every PR bumps the version.
teken cli doctor . --strict stays green in qodo-cli CI with the new verbs registered.

The rules guard against the PR fixer's recorded failure modes: same-repo, non-draft PRs only; the App's own comments (self_authored) and bot noise never start a run; one run per PR through a concurrency key; attempts are capped (docs/deliveries/2026-10-06-pr-fixer-rule.md:93, CHANGELOG.md:1107).
The rule conditions exist as configuration: head_repo equals base_repo, draft is false, self_authored is false, and a concurrency key per repo and PR number.

culture-rules connects surfaces and can call APIs, and it does not know the word qodo: no Qodo extension package, no Qodo action kind, no Qodo event namespace and no Qodo literal in culture_rules/. The configuration (actors, rules, workflows) knows Qodo and defines how to work with it. Anything culture-rules lacks to call the bridge is added as a generic capability.
Every capability added to culture-rules for this work is named and documented without reference to Qodo and is usable by another app.

No prompt lives in code. Instructions for the agent that improves the Qodo configuration are an actor brief (llm.complete) or step configuration (a bridge agent step's instruction), per CLAUDE.md 'No prompts in code' and docs/actors/llm.md:172-191.
No file in qodo-cli or culture-rules contains the improvement agent's instruction text; it is read from actor or step configuration at run time.

The bridge framework is assembled by citing culture-rules' generic parts into qodo-cli, since no shared reference for a server, an MCP server or a web shell exists: server/static.py (SPA serving), auth/access.py, resolve.py, tokens.py and principal.py (Cloudflare Access on loopback, service tokens on LAN, roles), mcp/server.py and tools.py with the verb registry and tests/test_surface_parity.py, the OpenAPI pin, hatch_build.py and web/src/culture-design. agentfront (formerly teken) derives only a CLI, a one-tool MCP and markdown pages, with no auth and no web app.
Each cited file in qodo-cli carries a header naming its culture-rules source path and commit, as xteink's access.py does.
The configuration PR opened for an improved Qodo configuration never starts another improvement run: no loop.
A test or a recorded live run shows a merged bridge-opened configuration PR starting no improvement run.
The options Qodo's API offers beyond rules search are reviewed, and the bridge's verbs are chosen from that review.
The verbs chosen for the bridge each trace to an entry in the recorded review of Qodo's docs (scope entry s14), and each MCP tool is confirmed with a live tools/list call before it is built on.
The bridge's API, MCP tools and CLI verbs are thin layers over one public Python API in qodo-cli, the qodo.api module that qodo-cli issue 18 asks for, so the three surfaces cannot drift.
No CLI handler, MCP tool or HTTP route in qodo-cli imports qodo.cli._providers or qodo.cli._qodo_api directly; they call qodo.api.

Improving Qodo after a merge can draw on Qodo's own record: the MCP tools review-history and similar-suggestions return past suggestions and whether they were accepted, and the changes land as repo files a PR can carry (.pr_agent.toml, and rule files Qodo imports on push).
A live call to Qodo's review-history tool returns accepted and rejected suggestions for at least one of our repos.

The operator who configures rules and workflows in culture-rules; agents (Pi first) that operate qodo-cli through its CLI or MCP server; and in-process integrators such as devex-cli (qodo-cli issue 18).
Each named audience has a documented way in: the editor and CLI for the operator, CLI and MCP for agents, qodo.api for integrators.

qodo-cli is a CLI a person or agent runs by hand under their own gh login. Qodo's findings are read by parsing the bot's comments, nothing happens when a PR opens or merges, and Qodo's configuration changes only when someone edits it. The previous bridge of this kind (jira-devague) needed a separate wrapper repo and live-only setup.
The before state matches qodo-cli main today: no listener, no MCP code, config verb limited to show, validate and init.

qodo-cli runs as a service with an API, an MCP server and a web UI over one Python API. Two configured culture-rules flows use it: after Qodo reviews an opened PR its findings are collected and triaged, and after a merge associate proposes an improved Qodo configuration, the bridge validates it, and culture-rules opens it as a PR through its GitHub App. culture-rules' code contains no Qodo-specific line.
The service runs as a unit on core and both flows are enabled there.

It sets the pattern for connecting an app to culture-rules without a wrapper repo or flow code in the engine: the app owns its API, MCP and UI, and culture-rules owns only configuration. The devague service planned to replace jira-devague is the next user of the pattern.
The bridge framework parts in qodo-cli contain no Qodo-specific code, so the next app can cite them as they are.
grep -ri qodo culture_rules/ returns 0 matches after the work, and tests/test_extension_boundary.py passes unchanged in its list of apps.
The grep is run in CI or recorded as evidence at delivery.
On 1 real same-repo PR, one workflow run started by Qodo's review ends 'succeeded' with the findings count the bridge returned, and the App's own comments start 0 runs.
The run id and the PR are recorded as delivery evidence.
After 1 merged PR, the improvement flow opens exactly 1 configuration PR, and merging that PR starts 0 improvement runs.
The two PRs and the run list are recorded as delivery evidence.
Every bridge verb is reachable 3 ways (CLI, MCP tool, HTTP operation) and a parity test fails when 1 of the 3 is missing.
The parity test is data-driven from the verb registry, so a new verb is covered without editing the test.

The bridge's first verbs cover: list a PR's findings from Qodo's MCP server, mark a finding implemented or dismiss it, search rules, read review history for a repo, and propose a configuration change, which validates the changed files and returns them for a workflow step to open as a PR.
Each verb has a CLI command, an MCP tool and an HTTP operation, and an explain catalog entry.

Every configuration PR is opened with a fixed branch prefix and a label, set in the workflow's step configuration and not by the agent, and the improvement rule's condition excludes PRs carrying that mark.
The mark is set by the bridge, not by the agent, so an agent cannot omit it.

The bridges never write to GitHub repositories: no push, no merge, no PR. A configuration change reaches a repo only as a PR that culture-rules' App opens on a repo in the App actor's allowlist, and that a person reviews and merges.
The qodo bridge has no merge call, and a request naming a repo outside the allowlist is refused before any GitHub request.

Text from PRs, Qodo findings and review history is untrusted input to the improvement agent. The qodo bridge's propose verb returns a change only when it touches paths in an allowlist of Qodo configuration files and the files validate, and refuses otherwise; the workflow opens a PR only from what the bridge returned.
A run whose checkout diff touches any other path produces no PR and a refusal the workflow can read.

The opened-PR flow starts from created events only (github.review.submitted, github.comment.created or github.review_comment.created by Qodo's login) and runs once per PR head commit, however many events one review produces. Re-reviews that edit an existing comment are out of the first version.
One Qodo review that posts 1 summary comment and several inline comments starts exactly 1 run for that head commit.
Bridge API responses meant for workflow steps are small: counts, ids, statuses and URLs, under the 64 KiB http.call body cap. Full findings stay in the bridge and its UI.
The findings verb's workflow-facing response for a PR with 100 findings is under 64 KiB.

At most 1 open configuration PR per repo: while one is open, a new improvement run for that repo ends without opening another. Improvement runs for one repo are serialized, and each run works in its own fresh checkout.
Two PRs merged in the same minute on one repo produce at most 1 open configuration PR.
The --json output of qodo-cli's existing verbs (rules, review, config, doctor) does not change shape; devex-cli binds to it in-process (qodo-cli issue 18).
The existing contract tests in tests/test_contracts.py pass unchanged.

Each bridge reports its own health: an unauthenticated health route with no secrets, a doctor check for the Qodo API key's presence and days to expiry, and a log of every PR it opened and every finding it changed.
doctor reports a failing check when the API key expires in fewer than 14 days.
No bridge route that reads findings, changes a finding or proposes a configuration change answers without authentication. culture-rules reaches the bridge with a service token held as a grant.
A request without a token to each such route returns 401.

Both flows can be stopped in one step and leave nothing behind: disabling the bundle's rules stops new runs, the bridges hold no state culture-rules depends on, and the bundle states the lowest culture-rules version it needs.
With the rules disabled, a PR open and a PR merge start 0 runs.

culture-rules gains one generic GitHub action that opens a PR as the App: given a repo in the actor's allowlist, a new branch name, file paths with contents, a title, a body and labels, it commits the files to the new branch (never the default branch) and opens the PR. Its name, params and docs do not mention Qodo, and it follows the all-surfaces rules for a new action kind (catalogue fixture, docs/actors/github.md, tests).
The action refuses a repo outside connection.repos and a branch equal to the default branch, and a retry of the same step opens no second PR.

tasks.summary: qodo-cli: rename the installed command from qodo to qodo-cli
acceptance_criteria: pyproject.toml [project.scripts] defines qodo-cli and no qodo entry; python -c 'import qodo' still works
learn, explain, overview, README and CLAUDE.md name the command qodo-cli; tests/test_cli.py and tests/test_contracts.py pass with --json shapes unchanged
tasks.instruction: Repo ../qodo-cli. Merge or rebase onto the docs/readme-rewrite work first, since it rewrites the README. Change only the entry point and the self-description strings; keep the import package name qodo. Bump the version with the version-bump skill.

tasks.summary: qodo-cli: probe Qodo's MCP server live and record its tool schemas
acceptance_criteria: docs/qodo-mcp-tools.md lists each tool the bridge will use (findings, mark-implemented, dismiss, rules search/list/get, review-history) with the input schema returned by a real tools/list call
tests/fixtures/ holds one recorded response per tool, with secrets and private text removed
the doc states, from a real call or Qodo's current configuration reference, whether best_practices.md and [pr_reviewer] extra_instructions are still read
tasks.instruction: Needs the operator's Qodo API key in QODO_API_KEY; do not commit or log it. Endpoint and auth are in the spec's scope entry on Qodo's docs (Streamable HTTP, Bearer key, trailing slash). If a tool the spec names does not exist, stop and report it rather than substituting another.

tasks.summary: qodo-cli: public Python API qodo.api over the existing logic
acceptance_criteria: qodo/api.py exposes review_list, review_resolve, rules_get and config show/validate/init returning plain objects, as qodo-cli issue 18 asks
the CLI handlers for rules, review and config call qodo.api; a test fails if a handler imports qodo.cli._providers or qodo.cli._qodo_api
tests/test_contracts.py passes unchanged
tasks.instruction: Move, do not rewrite: the logic in qodo/cli/_providers.py and qodo/cli/_qodo_api.py becomes importable through qodo.api. Stdlib only.

tasks.summary: qodo-cli: the upstream gateway, a client for Qodo's MCP server and rules API behind an exposure policy
acceptance_criteria: one gateway module lists Qodo's tools and calls any of them by name over MCP, and wraps the rules search API; an exposure policy held in configuration names each upstream tool that is exposed, the verb name it gets and the surfaces it appears on, and anything not named is refused

the gateway is stdlib only, refuses a non-HTTPS endpoint, never prints the API key, and refuses a tool whose annotation says it is not read-only unless the policy marks it as an allowed write; tested against the recorded schemas and fixtures
qodo.api gains findings_list(pr_url), findings_implement(ids), findings_dismiss(ids, reason), rules_search, rules_list and review_history(repo, path), each a thin call through the gateway
tasks.instruction: One module for the MCP transport (JSON-RPC over Streamable HTTP with urllib; the reply is an event stream whose last data line is the response; there is no session id), one for the policy, one for the qodo.api functions. Follow docs/qodo-mcp-tools.md and tests/fixtures/qodo_mcp/, not the spec's guesses: findings are addressed by PR URL, changes are batched by finding_ids, dismiss needs a reason, history needs a file path. Every upstream tool carries readOnlyHint and destructiveHint annotations; use them for the default-deny rule. The history tools were failing upstream when probed; build them against the schema and mark their tests as schema-only.

tasks.summary: qodo-cli: the verb registry, built from the exposure policy plus the local verbs, and the CLI verbs it yields
acceptance_criteria: one registry lists every bridge verb with its params schema: each upstream tool the policy exposes becomes a verb whose params come from the recorded input schema, beside the local verbs; the shipped policy exposes findings list, findings implement, findings dismiss, rules search, rules list, rules get and history show, and no tool that writes to a pull request or changes a rule
each verb has a CLI command with --json, CliError failures, an explain catalog entry and a mention in learn and overview; teken cli doctor . --strict is green
findings list --summary prints counts, ids, statuses and URLs only, and its JSON for a 100-finding fixture is under 64 KiB
tasks.instruction: Cite culture-rules' registry shape (culture_rules/cli/registry.py and cli/verbs) with a provenance header. config propose is a separate task; register its name here and leave the handler to that task.

tasks.summary: qodo-cli: config propose validates a change and returns it
acceptance_criteria: given a checkout and a base ref, config propose returns the changed files with contents only when every changed path is in the configured allowlist of Qodo configuration files and the files validate
a diff touching any other path, or an invalid file, returns a refusal with a reason and no file contents
the bridge's own repo allowlist refuses a repo outside it before any other work; no code path in qodo-cli pushes, merges or opens a PR
tasks.instruction: Validation follows what the probe task found about current versus legacy settings. The path allowlist and repo allowlist are configuration, not constants.

tasks.summary: qodo-cli: cite the bridge framework parts from culture-rules
acceptance_criteria: qodo/bridge/ holds the cited auth (access, resolve, tokens, principal), static serving and caching modules, each with a header naming its culture-rules source path and commit
no file under qodo/bridge/ contains the word qodo outside its import paths and provenance header, checked by a test
pyproject.toml gains server and mcp extras; a test in an environment without them shows zero third-party packages installed and every existing verb working
tasks.instruction: Sources: culture_rules/server/static.py, server/caching.py, auth/access.py, auth/resolve.py, auth/tokens.py, auth/principal.py, auth/guards.py. Replace the CULTURE_RULES_ env prefix with a parameter so a second app can cite the same files. Rewrite the route-to-role policy; do not copy culture-rules' route matrix.

tasks.summary: qodo-cli: the HTTP API (qodo-cli serve)
acceptance_criteria: serve starts loopback and LAN listeners; every registry verb is an HTTP operation, an upstream tool the policy does not expose is unreachable on every surface, and api/openapi.json is pinned by a test
a request without a token to each route that reads findings, changes a finding or proposes a change returns 401; GET /health answers without a token and carries no secret
serve runs from an installed wheel with no Node on the machine
tasks.instruction: FastAPI and uvicorn behind the server extra, imported lazily. Handlers call qodo.api only.

tasks.summary: qodo-cli: the MCP server (qodo-cli mcp) and the surface parity test
acceptance_criteria: mcp serves one tool per registry verb, so an exposed upstream tool is proxied under the name the policy gives it and an unexposed one is absent
a data-driven parity test checks every registry verb has a CLI command, an MCP tool and an HTTP operation, and fails when one is missing
tasks.instruction: Cite culture_rules/mcp/server.py, mcp/tools.py and tests/test_surface_parity.py with provenance headers. The mcp SDK sits behind the mcp extra.

tasks.summary: qodo-cli: health, key expiry and a change log
acceptance_criteria: doctor reports a failing check when the Qodo API key is missing or expires in fewer than 14 days, and passes otherwise
every finding change and every proposed configuration change appends one line to a log the UI can read
tasks.instruction: Key expiry is not readable from the key itself; take the expiry date from configuration set when the key is created, and say so in doctor's remediation text.

tasks.summary: qodo-cli: web shell, wheel build and CI for the UI
acceptance_criteria: web/ holds a React app whose header and tokens match the design canvas; hatch_build.py ships its build inside the wheel and serve returns it at /
CI has a web job (install, typecheck, unit tests) and publish.yml builds the UI and triggers on web/** as well as qodo/**
tasks.instruction: Cite culture-rules' hatch_build.py, web/src/culture-design and the API client shape, with provenance headers. The canvas https://claude.ai/artifact/JQLGKoX2zDwQKnSUQxFyWB is the visual reference; its data is sample content.

tasks.summary: qodo-cli: the three UI screens (Findings, Configuration, Rules)
acceptance_criteria: Findings lists open PRs by repo and shows a PR's findings with Mark implemented and Dismiss calling the API; Configuration shows each repo's files, validation result and proposed change; Rules searches rules with a repo scope
each screen works at phone width and by keyboard, with component tests against fixture data
tasks.instruction: Follow the canvas artboards Main, Configuration and Rules. Fields come from the schemas the probe task recorded; drop any field on the canvas that Qodo does not return and report it.

tasks.summary: associate: cite the bridge framework and add the server and mcp extras
acceptance_criteria: associate/bridge/ holds the same cited auth and static-serving modules as qodo-cli, each with a provenance header, and no file there contains app-specific code
pip install with no extras still installs zero third-party packages and every existing verb works
tasks.instruction: Repo ../associate, source version 0.10.0 on branch spec/associate-multi-model-on-pi, which has an open plan and an uncommitted culture.yaml edit: branch from wherever the operator says and do not touch culture.yaml, associate/harness/pi.py or gate.json. Cite from qodo-cli's qodo/bridge/ as landed by the qodo-cli framework task, keeping the culture-rules provenance.

tasks.summary: associate: runs API, start a run and read its result
acceptance_criteria: runs start takes a checkout, a model, an instruction and test commands and returns a run id at once; runs show returns status and, when finished, outcome, merge, tests.passed, the base commit and the changed paths, in under 64 KiB
a second start for a checkout with a run in progress is refused; a run that exits 0 with a refused merge or failing tests reports failure, not success
each verb is a CLI command, an HTTP operation behind a token, and has an explain catalog entry; GET /health needs no token
tasks.instruction: Wrap the existing synchronous associate run as a detached process, the way .pi/extensions/associate/tools/delegate.ts does, and store state outside the checkout. associate run commits and merges into the checkout's local main when the run is ok and tests pass; report that, and never push. Update the four places a new verb needs (command module, parser, explain catalog, learn).

tasks.summary: associate: MCP server and the surface parity test
acceptance_criteria: mcp serves one tool per registry verb, and a data-driven parity test fails when a verb lacks a CLI command, an MCP tool or an HTTP operation
tasks.instruction: Same cited modules as the qodo-cli MCP task.

tasks.summary: associate: web UI, a runs list and a run page
acceptance_criteria: the operator confirmed a design artboard for the two screens before any UI code was written
the UI ships in the wheel, lists runs with status and outcome, and a run page shows its statements, tests and changed paths
tasks.instruction: No design exists for associate's UI yet. Add artboards to the same canvas, in the same tokens, and get the operator's confirmation first.

tasks.summary: culture-rules: a generic GitHub action that opens a PR as the App
acceptance_criteria: the action takes actor, repo, branch, base, files (path and content), title, body and labels; it commits the files to the new branch and opens the PR, returning number, url and head sha

it refuses a repo outside connection.repos, a branch equal to the default branch and an action not listed in params.actions; when the branch already exists it opens nothing and returns skipped with the open PR's number
a retried step opens no second PR; the kind is in the action catalogue fixture, docs/actors/github.md and the extension tests; grep -ri qodo culture_rules/ returns nothing
tasks.instruction: Inside culture_rules/extensions/github only: client calls for a ref, a tree or contents commit and a pull, a port, the kind with its ParamSpecs and a params validator. Follow github.comment's once-claim pattern for idempotency. Regenerate web/src/fixtures/action-kinds.data.ts. The working tree on main holds unrelated uncommitted button-code work in extensions/github/merge.py and extensions/discord: start from a clean worktree under ../.worktrees.culture-rules/.

tasks.summary: qodo-cli: the culture-rules bundle (actors, rules, workflows), shipped disabled
acceptance_criteria: a bundle directory imports cleanly with culture-rules rollout import --bundle and every rule in it is disabled; it states the lowest culture-rules version it needs
the findings rule fires on created Qodo review and comment events for same-repo, non-draft PRs, never on self_authored events, and a keyset step makes it run once per PR head commit

the improvement rule fires on github.pr.closed with merged true, excludes head branches carrying the configuration prefix, runs one at a time per repo, and opens the PR with a fixed branch name and label set as literals in step configuration
the agent's instruction text appears only in the bundle's step or actor configuration; with the rules disabled a PR open and a PR merge start no run
tasks.instruction: Steps are http.call to the two bridges, retry_until to wait for the associate run, the keyset built-ins, and the open-PR action. A fixed branch name gives the one-open-PR rule through the action's skipped result. Labels are not in GitHub event data, so the loop guard is the branch prefix in a contains condition. Test the bundle against a MemoryStore engine with recorded events.

tasks.summary: qodo-cli and associate: documentation for the three audiences
acceptance_criteria: qodo-cli's README, CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.colleague.md describe the bridge; docs cover the operator (running the service, the bundle), agents (CLI and MCP) and integrators (qodo.api)
associate's README and CLAUDE.md describe its bridge surfaces; markdownlint passes in both repos
tasks.instruction: Docs describe what is on disk. Call the app a bridge and say once that this is not the cultureagent agent-session bridge.

tasks.summary: deploy both bridges on core and configure culture-rules
acceptance_criteria: both services run as units on core with their secrets held as grants, and their health routes answer
the GitHub App has contents and pull-request write on the allowlisted repos, the App actor lists the new action, and its pinned digest is updated
the bundle is imported and its rules are enabled

tasks.summary: live verification of both flows and the evidence
acceptance_criteria: on 1 real same-repo PR one run started by Qodo's review ends succeeded with the findings count, and the App's own comments started 0 runs; run id and PR recorded
after 1 merged PR exactly 1 configuration PR was opened, and merging it started 0 improvement runs; both PRs and the run list recorded
grep -ril qodo culture_rules/ prints nothing and tests/test_extension_boundary.py passes; no repository was created
tasks.instruction: File each result with devague evidence against the matching obligation.

risks.text: associate's source is 0.10.0 on an unmerged branch with an open plan and an uncommitted culture.yaml edit; the installed 0.9.0 lacks --model. The associate tasks need that branch merged or a base the operator names.

associate run merges into the checkout's local main and exits 0 even when the merge is refused or tests fail; the checkout used by the flow must be a dedicated clone, and callers must read outcome, merge and tests.
associate does no writes unless the lobes decider and the cortex model are reachable with ASSOCIATE_API_KEY; cortex is served from spark and the services run on core.
Qodo's MCP tools and settings are known only from doc summaries until the probe task runs; a missing tool changes the verb list.

Checked during t17: the pinned digest of the github-app actor (culture_rules/actors/trusted.py, _actor_projection) does not cover params.actions or repos, so listing the new action on the live actor changes no digest and needs no release. The remaining point is that github.pr_open does not require a pinned actor, as github.comment does not.
No design exists for associate's web UI; the operator has confirmed only the qodo canvas.
Whether Qodo's terms allow one person's API key to back a shared service is unanswered.

Qodo's history tools (pull-request-review-history, similar-suggestions, stats) failed twice with MT-UPSTREAM-DOWN on 2026-11-16; no successful reply has been seen, so target c26/h12 has no evidence and the improvement flow's input from review history is unproven.

t2 recorded no reply for pr-review-mark-implemented or pr-review-dismiss: Qodo marks both destructive and a call changes a real finding, so only their input schemas are known; and whether Qodo still reads best_practices.md and [pr_reviewer] extra_instructions is unverified (absent from its current docs). t2's second and third acceptance criteria are therefore only partly met
